issues.t: Radiator leaks coolant into the transmission
issues.sym: Shudder, slipping or harsh shifts, a flashing or lit check engine light, and transmission fluid that looks pink and milky. Sometimes coolant loss too.
issues.why: The transmission fluid cooler is built into the bottom of the radiator. When it cracks inside, coolant mixes with the transmission fluid and ruins the clutches.
issues.next: Have the transmission fluid checked for coolant right away. If it is caught early, a new radiator and several fluid flushes may save the transmission; many owners fit a separate transmission cooler.

issues.sym: A whine, hiss or rattle at startup that may fade as the engine warms. Later the check engine light, a loss of power, shaking or stalling.
issues.why: Timing chain parts on the early direct-injection 5.6L V8 wear out. Infiniti ran a service campaign (P6305) for timing chain repairs on some 2011-2013 QX56s. Owners report failures from about 70,000 miles.
issues.next: Ask an Infiniti dealer to check your VIN for campaign P6305. Don't ignore a startup whine; a failed chain can wreck the engine.

issues.sym: A rattle or whine from the front of the engine, a check engine light for cam timing, rough running or lost power, usually past 100,000 miles.
issues.why: On the first 5.6L V8 the timing chain stretches with mileage and wears its tensioners and guides.
issues.next: Have a shop check cam timing codes and listen at startup. Replace chains and guides before the chain jumps.

issues.sym: A ticking noise loudest on a cold engine, an exhaust smell, a louder exhaust or a check engine light.
issues.why: The 5.6L V8's cast exhaust manifolds crack from repeated heating and cooling. It is common on Nissan's big V8 trucks and SUVs, and less frequent on 2017 and newer models.
issues.next: Have the manifolds inspected. Exhaust leaks near the engine can let fumes into the cabin and can damage the catalytic converters.

issues.sym: A check engine light, often with code P0430 or P0420, sometimes with weak acceleration or a rotten-egg smell.
issues.why: Owners report both catalytic converters failing between about 70,000 and 150,000 miles, sometimes much sooner.
issues.next: Have the codes and oxygen sensors checked first. Ask about emissions warranty coverage, which on converters can run 8 years or 80,000 miles.

issues.t: Rusted rear control arm or subframe
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the SUV wandering at highway speed, or in the worst cases a rear wheel breaking loose.
issues.why: Owners in salt-belt states report severe rust on the rear control arms and rear subframe, leading to cracks and failure.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension and subframe inspected on a lift every year, especially in snowy areas. Do not drive it if parts are cracked.

issues.sym: The rear end sits low, especially after parking overnight, the compressor runs a lot or the SUV squats when stopping.
issues.why: The rear load-leveling air suspension has air springs, lines, a compressor and height sensors that leak or wear with age.
issues.next: Have the air springs and lines leak-tested. Replacing failed parts or converting to regular coil springs are both options.

issues.sym: Oil seeping from the top of the engine, a burning oil smell or light smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The two valve cover gaskets get brittle and crack with age, usually after about 10 years or 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Replace both gaskets. Fix it before oil drips onto the hot exhaust.

issues.t: Engine may stall from a faulty relay (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start.
issues.why: The engine computer relay inside the fuse box (IPDM) could build up a coating on its contacts from arcing, cutting power to the engine computer.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer fixes it free.

issues.t: Fuel gauge shows fuel when the tank is empty (recall)
issues.sym: The gauge reads about a quarter tank and the engine runs out of fuel and stalls.
issues.why: A fault in the fuel gauge sending system could make the gauge read higher than the real fuel level.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Until it is fixed, refill well before the gauge gets low.

issues.t: A/C condenser fan motor may overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell from the front of the SUV, or the A/C fan not running.
issues.why: Water could get into the A/C condenser fan motor and corrode it, which could make it overheat and start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the fan motor replaced free.

issues.t: Brake pedal pivot pin may slip (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels loose or out of place.
issues.why: The pin the brake pedal pivots on might not be formed correctly and could slide out, partly disconnecting the pedal.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If the pedal feels odd, do not drive it.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag may be blocked by trim (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms.
issues.why: On SUVs built in one week in February 2007, a front pillar trim panel could get in the way of the side curtain airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the trim free.

issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: A manufacturing problem could make the driver airbag inflator rupture when it deploys, sending metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the inflator replaced free as soon as possible.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator has a wrong part (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: On some SUVs built from late 2012 to 2013, an incorrect part in the driver airbag inflator could make it rupture.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the inflator free.

issues.sym: A smell of gasoline from the engine bay.
issues.why: The fuel pressure sensors were not tightened enough at the factory and could loosen and leak fuel, a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If you smell fuel, stop driving and have it checked.

issues.sym: Clear coat or paint peeling from the roof, hood or body panels.
issues.why: Peeling paint is the most-reported complaint on the 2011 QX56 on CarComplaints. Owners say repairs were refused after the warranty.
issues.next: Ask an Infiniti dealer about goodwill help, with photos. A body shop refinish is the usual fix.

issues.sym: Shudder or vibration at light throttle and low rpm, especially uphill, along with hesitation or jerky downshifts.
issues.why: The 7-speed automatic's torque converter can shudder. Infiniti issued bulletins with engine and transmission software updates, and some cars need a new torque converter.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for transmission bulletins and software updates. Note when it happens so they can repeat it.

issues.sym: The fuel gauge falls to half a tank after a short drive, then catches up later.
issues.why: A known fault on these years. Infiniti released a bulletin that replaces the gauge cluster with an updated one.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the gauge cluster bulletin. Track your miles per tank until it is fixed.

issues.t: Battery drains and the SUV won't start
issues.sym: The battery goes flat after sitting, the engine sounds like it tries to start but doesn't turn over, or it needs jump starts again and again.
issues.why: Owners report repeated dead batteries, especially on short trips; the charging system doesn't fully recharge the battery. Infiniti issued a bulletin on this.
issues.next: Have the battery, charging system and parasitic draw tested. Ask the dealer about the battery and charging bulletins.

issues.t: Emergency braking activates for no reason
issues.sym: The SUV brakes hard on its own with nothing in front of it.
issues.why: Owners report the forward emergency braking system triggering false stops. Dealers often cannot reproduce it.
issues.next: Note when and where it happens and report it to the dealer and NHTSA. Keep the front radar sensor clean.

issues.sym: A loud bang and the sunroof glass breaks while driving or parked, with no sign of anything hitting it.
issues.why: Owners of several model years, including the new 2025-2026 QX80, report sunroof or panoramic roof glass shattering on its own.
issues.next: Pull over safely and cover the opening. Report it to Infiniti and NHTSA, and check whether the warranty or your insurance covers the glass.

issues.sym: One or both center screens go black or keep restarting, taking the radio, navigation, phone and cameras with them.
issues.why: A software or control unit fault in the dual-screen system introduced for 2020.
issues.next: Hold the audio power button for about 10 seconds to reset it. If it keeps happening, ask the dealer for a software update or unit replacement.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: No rear camera picture when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Camera display settings could be changed in a way that stops the rearview image from showing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer updates the software free.

issues.sym: The screen stays blank in reverse.
issues.why: A software error could stop the display from showing the rearview image.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer updates the software free.

issues.sym: The engine runs rough, loses power or stalls, and may not restart.
issues.why: The fuel pump's plastic impeller can swell and rub, causing the pump to stop.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the fuel pump free.

issues.t: Rear camera may freeze or show a blank screen (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture freezes or the screen is blank when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Two software errors in the new QX80's infotainment and Around View Monitor could freeze or blank the rearview image.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recalls; the fix is a free software update by the dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Rear camera may not show after startup (recall)
issues.sym: No rear camera picture in reverse after starting the SUV.
issues.why: A software error at startup in the infotainment system can stop the rearview image from showing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the fix is a free software update.

issues.sym: The center screens freeze or restart while driving, sometimes blanking the gauge cluster, cutting the A/C or blasting the audio.
issues.why: Owners of the new-generation QX80 report repeated infotainment software crashes.
issues.next: Make sure all software updates are done. Report repeat cases to the dealer and NHTSA.

issues.sym: A 'Malfunction - See Owner's Manual' warning for the safety systems, lane keeping or ProPilot Assist steering or braking abruptly, or switching off with little warning.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the camera and radar based driver-assist systems on the new QX80; one dealer replaced an ADAS control module.
issues.next: Keep your hands on the wheel and be ready to take over. Have the dealer scan the driver-assist modules and check for updates.

issues.t: Wrong axle weight on the door label (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. Affects SUVs with 22-inch wheels.
issues.why: The certification label lists the wrong axle weight rating, so the SUV could be loaded more than it should be.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer installs a corrected label free. Don't overload the SUV in the meantime.

issues.t: Power liftgate won't open or close
issues.sym: The rear power liftgate stops partway, reverses, or will not open or close.
issues.why: A rear power door that does not work properly is one of the reported QX56 problems. Struts, motors or switches can fail.
issues.next: Have the liftgate motor, struts and switches checked. Weak struts are the simplest thing to replace first.
